passages.heading: MD&A
passages.text: The following discussion of our financial condition and results of operations is based upon and should be read in conjunction with our consolidated financial statements and their related notes included in this annual report on Form 20-F. This annual report contains forward-looking statements. See “Forward-Looking Statement.” In evaluating our business, you should carefully consider the information provided under the caption “Item 3. Key Information—D. Risk Factors” in this annual report. We caution you that our businesses and financial performance are subject to substantial risks and uncertainties. A. Operating Results We are a leading one-stop travel service provider globally, integrating a comprehensive suite of travel products and services and differentiated travel content. We are the go-to destination for travelers in Asia, and increasingly for travelers around the world, to explore travel and get inspired, to make informed and cost-effective travel bookings, and to enjoy hassle-free, on-the-go support and share travel experience. In 2025, we derived approximately 42% of our total revenues from our accommodation reservation, 36% from transportation ticketing, 7% from packaged tour, 5% from corporate travel, and 10% from other products and services. Major Factors Affecting Our Results of Operations Economy and travel industry trends As a leading travel service provider globally, our business is driven by the demand for travel services in our key markets. Demand for travel services primarily depends on the growth of the economy. Economic growth generally stimulates willingness to pay for travel services and their affordability, thus helping increase travel frequency and spending. We also benefit from certain other key trends in the travel industry that affect how and how often users choose to purchase travel services, such as the increasing consumption potential in the rising middle class, user preference for diverse travel options, the booming demand for high-quality travel experience, and technology-driven enhancement in the travel industry supply chain. Our business and results of operations can be adversely affected by disruptions in the travel industry, such as (i) the outbreaks of pandemics, epidemics, or fear of spread of contagious diseases, (ii) geopolitical uncertainty, political unrest, or civil strife, (iii) natural disasters or poor weather conditions, such as hurricanes, earthquakes, or tsunamis, and (iv) any travel restrictions or other security procedures implemented in connection with any major events in key markets. 78 Table of Contents The depth and breadth of our travel offerings Our results of operations depend on the effectiveness of our product and service offerings and our ability to broaden our offerings to appeal to a wider audience and fuel our GMV growth. We offer a comprehensive suite of travel products and services leveraging our network of ecosystem partners. Our relationships with our expanding pool of ecosystem partners enable us to provide a diverse selection of travel offerings from budget to premium products and services, including long-tail and customized products, to satisfy the needs of our user base.

passages.heading: Risk factors
passages.text: Summary of Risk Factors An investment in our ADSs or ordinary shares involves significant risks. The operational and legal risks as well as the potential consequences associated with being based in and having operations in the Chinese mainland as discussed in the risk factors under “Item 3. Key Information—D. Risk Factors—Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry” also apply to operations in Hong Kong and Macao. Below is a summary of material risks we face, organized under their headings. These risks are discussed more fully in “Item 3. Key Information—D. Risk Factors.” Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry • Our business could suffer if we do not successfully manage our future developments, or if we are unable to execute our strategies effectively. For more details, see “Risk Factors—Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry—Our business could suffer if we do not successfully manage our future developments, or if we are unable to execute our strategies effectively.” • General declines or disruptions in the travel industry may materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations. For more details, see “Risk Factors—Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry—General declines or disruptions in the travel industry may materially and adversely affect our business and results of operations.” • If we are unable to maintain existing relationships with ecosystem partners and strategic alliances, or unable to establish new arrangements with ecosystem partners and strategic alliances at or on favorable terms or at terms similar to those we currently have, or at all, our business, market share, and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected. For more details, see “Risk Factors—Risks Relating to Our Business and Industry—If we are unable to maintain existing relationships with ecosystem partners and strategic alliances, or unable to establish new arrangements with ecosystem partners and strategic alliances at or on favorable terms or at terms similar to those we currently have, or at all, our business, market share, and results of operations may be materially and adversely affected.” • If we do not compete successfully against new and existing competitors, we may lose our market share, and our business may be materially and adversely affected. credit_strengths.text: TCOM's net cash position, with unrestricted cash exceeding total debt, provides a substantial liquidity buffer and supports a minimal indicative financial risk profile. The company's cash balance covers debt comfortably, and net leverage is negative, indicating a conservative capital structure relative to the sector median. This financial flexibility underpins credit resilience.

Operating cash flow remains robust, covering debt service multiple times over. Interest coverage is exceptionally high, well above the sector median, reflecting ample capacity to meet interest obligations. Free cash flow to debt also exceeds sector norms, underscoring strong internal cash generation relative to borrowings.

key_risks.text: TCOM's business is highly exposed to travel demand volatility, as disclosed in risk factors. General declines or disruptions in the travel industry, whether from pandemics, geopolitical unrest, or natural disasters, could materially and adversely affect results. This cyclicality poses a key risk to revenue and cash flow stability, potentially weakening debt servicing capacity during downturns.

A significant portion of debt is classified as current, indicating refinancing concentration. While the company holds substantial cash, a large current debt maturity requires active management. The debt structure includes both long-term and short-term components, and any refinancing difficulty could strain liquidity, especially if cash flows deteriorate.

debt_servicing_capacity.text: Interest coverage is exceptionally strong, with operating income covering interest expense many times over. This provides a large cushion against earnings volatility. The company's operating margin also exceeds the sector median, indicating efficient operations that support debt servicing. However, interest expense is a small portion of overall costs, so coverage remains sensitive to operating income swings.

Free cash flow to debt is healthy, and operating cash flow consistently exceeds capital expenditures, generating surplus cash for debt reduction or shareholder returns. The company's net cash position further enhances debt servicing capacity. Nevertheless, cash flow has trended lower recently, and a sustained decline could pressure coverage metrics, warranting monitoring.

overall_credit_view.text: TCOM exhibits a strong credit profile, characterized by net cash, high interest coverage, and robust operating cash flow. The indicative financial risk profile is minimal, with leverage below sector median and ample liquidity. The company's market position in travel services supports revenue generation, though cyclicality remains a consideration. Overall, credit fundamentals are solid.

Forward-looking, TCOM's ability to manage travel demand fluctuations and refinance current debt will be key. Shareholder distributions absorb a portion of free cash flow, but the net cash position provides a buffer. The company is well-positioned to withstand sector downturns, though a material travel disruption could pressure metrics. Analyst judgement: stable outlook with low credit risk.

credit_strengths.text: TCOM的淨現金狀況，即不受限制現金超過總債務，提供了充裕的流動性緩衝，並支持極低的指示性財務風險狀況。公司的現金餘額輕鬆覆蓋債務，且淨槓桿為負，表明相對於行業中位數，其資本結構保守。這種財務靈活性支撐了信用韌性。
營運現金流保持強勁，足以多次覆蓋債務償付。利息覆蓋率極高，遠高於行業中位數，反映其有充足能力履行利息義務。自由現金流對債務比率亦超過行業常規，凸顯相對於借款的強勁內部現金生成能力。

key_risks.text: 如風險因素所披露，TCOM的業務高度暴露於旅遊需求波動。旅遊行業的普遍下滑或中斷，無論是源於疫情、地緣政治動盪還是自然災害，都可能對業績造成重大不利影響。這種週期性對收入和現金流穩定性構成關鍵風險，可能在低迷時期削弱債務償付能力。
相當大一部分債務被歸類為流動負債，表明再融資集中。儘管公司持有大量現金，但大額流動債務到期需要積極管理。債務結構包括長期和短期組成部分，任何再融資困難都可能使流動性承壓，尤其是在現金流惡化的情況下。

debt_servicing_capacity.text: 利息覆蓋率異常強勁，營運收入覆蓋利息支出的倍數極高。這為盈利波動提供了巨大緩衝。公司的營運利潤率亦超過行業中位數，表明營運效率支持債務償付。然而，利息支出僅佔總成本的一小部分，因此覆蓋率仍對營運收入波動敏感。
自由現金流對債務比率穩健，且營運現金流持續超過資本支出，產生盈餘現金用於削減債務或股東回報。公司的淨現金狀況進一步增強了債務償付能力。儘管如此，現金流近期呈下降趨勢，若持續下降可能對覆蓋率指標構成壓力，值得監測。

overall_credit_view.text: TCOM展現出強勁的信用狀況，其特點是淨現金、高利息覆蓋率和穩健的營運現金流。指示性財務風險狀況為極低，槓桿低於行業中位數且流動性充裕。公司在旅遊服務領域的市場地位支持收入生成，儘管週期性仍是一項考量因素。總體而言，信用基本面穩固。
前瞻性來看，TCOM管理旅遊需求波動和為流動債務再融資的能力將是關鍵。股東分派吸收了部分自由現金流，但淨現金狀況提供了緩衝。公司處於有利地位，能夠抵禦行業低迷，儘管重大旅遊中斷可能對指標構成壓力。分析師判斷：展望穩定，信用風險低。
